reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Quarterly mineral statements and per-ton inspection fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)-(15)) and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 5, A.L. 1984 H.B. 1317, A.L. 2023 S.B. 109). Requires commercial mineral operators to file sworn quarterly disposition statements within 30 days after each quarter with the director and DOR division of taxation and collection and pay non-exhaustive per-ton inspection fees on listed primary products (lead, zinc, coal, clays, shale, copper, iron ore, silica, granite, rhyolite, manganese, and cobalt).

headings.title: Adding chemical-equivalent minerals and fees after commission approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (1959-2023 amendments). Directs the director, contingent upon labor and industrial relations commission approval, to announce newly mined chemical-equivalent minerals and associated fees by published notice, taking effect 60 days after publication and added to a regulation.

headings.title: Minimum quarterly mine inspection fee
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (1959-2023 amendments). Notwithstanding subsections 1 and 2, requires every commercial mineral operator to pay a minimum $25 mine inspection fee within 30 days after each quarter.

headings.title: Creation of State Mine Inspection Fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (1959-2023 amendments). Creates the "State Mine Inspection Fund" in the state treasury for deposit of section 293.030 mine inspection fees.

headings.title: Agency access to production, shipment, and sales records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (1959-2023 amendments). Grants the director and DOR division of taxation and collection access to tonnage, footage, shipment, and sales records of chapter-subject operators, their vendees and vendees' agents, and carriers to verify required statements.

headings.title: Discretionary late fees and collection lawsuits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (1959-2023 amendments). Authorizes a 10% late fee for fees unpaid within 30 days after a quarter and permits the director to sue in the mine's county circuit court or Cole County circuit court to collect unpaid fees, late fees, interest, and direct collection attorney fees and costs.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 6 subsections (including sub 1 subdivisions (1)-(15)) and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 5, A.L. 1984 H.B. 1317, A.L. 2023 S.B. 109) and verified all fingerprints. Checked commercial mineral operator statements and non-exhaustive per-ton fees in sub 1, labor and industrial relations commission approval condition before published notice/60-day effective date/regulation addition in sub 2, $25 quarterly minimum notwithstanding subs 1-2 in sub 3, State Mine Inspection Fund creation in sub 4, agency record access in sub 5, and discretionary 10% late fees and circuit-court collection suits in sub 6. Revised sub 2 title to reflect the mandatory commission approval contingency; retained subs 1 and 3-6.

headings.title: Eight-hour workday limit without employee consent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 7). Declares eight hours to constitute a day for mining or mineral prospecting employees and makes working an employee longer than eight hours in a 24-hour day unlawful without the employee's consent.

headings.title: Compliance with chapter and reasonable safety rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 7). Requires operators and employees to comply with chapter 293, cooperate with the division of mine inspection, and obey reasonable safety rules and regulations in harmony with the chapter.

headings.title: Posting and protection of law and rule abstracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 7). Directs the director to furnish abstracts of chapter 293 and authorized rules for conspicuous posting at or near mines, makes removal or defacement unlawful, and requires operators to renew obliterated or destroyed abstracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 7) and verified all fingerprints. Checked eight-hour workday limit qualified by employee consent in sub 1, operator/employee chapter compliance and reasonable safety rules in sub 2, and furnished/posted abstracts, defacement prohibition, and operator renewal in sub 3. Retained all 3 drafted titles.

headings.title: Sanitation and washrooms for twenty-five or more underground
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 10). Requires operators of mines employing 25 or more men underground to maintain a sanitary washroom and dressing room near the principal entrance plus other sanitation facilities required by the director.

headings.title: First aid equipment locations and protective containers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 10). Requires every mine to maintain adequate first aid supplies on the surface and at strategic underground locations in reasonably dusttight, moistureproof sanitary receptacles.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 10) and verified all fingerprints. Checked the 25-or-more underground worker applicability threshold for washrooms, dressing rooms, and director-required sanitation facilities in sub 1 and universal surface/underground first aid equipment and dusttight/moistureproof containers in sub 2. Revised sub 1 title to preserve the 25-or-more underground threshold; retained sub 2.

headings.title: Securing working places against roof, rib, and face falls
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 12). Requires all working places to be sufficiently secured to protect face workers from roof, rib, or face falls, and requires loose or overhanging top, faces, and ribs to be adequately supported or taken down.

headings.title: Traveling ways at shaft bottoms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 12). Requires a traveling way at the bottom of every shaft so workers can cross sides without passing under or over cages.

headings.title: Sanitary drinking devices in mines employing ten or more
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 12). Requires owners, agents, or operators of mines employing 10 or more men to provide sanitary drinking devices for employees.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 12) and verified all fingerprints. Verified face/roof/rib fall protection in sub 1, shaft-bottom traveling ways in sub 2, and sanitary drinking devices for mines employing 10 or more men in sub 3. Retained all 3 drafted titles.

headings.title: Haulage tracks, locomotives, signals, and rolling stock
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 14). Sets construction, maintenance, brake, sand-rigging, audible-warning, headlight, trip-light/reflector, and hazard-prevention requirements for mine haulage tracks, locomotives, shuttle cars, trucks, and other rolling stock.

headings.title: Safeguards for underground gasoline engines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 14). Prohibits underground use of gasoline engines unless equipped with proper safeguards preventing gas emissions that contaminate air beyond section 293.120 limits.

headings.title: Restrictions on riding locomotives and haulage cars
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 14). Restricts locomotive riding to the motorman, trip rider, or persons authorized by the mine foreman, and bars riding on loaded cars or between cars except the trip rider on the last car.

headings.title: Man-trip speed and passenger limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 14). Prohibits running man trips faster than the speed determined by the director or carrying more men per car than ordered by the director.

headings.title: Uniform haulage signals and traffic control systems
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 14). Requires each mine or mines operated to adopt uniform haulage signals and a traffic control system with which all haulage crews must comply.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 14) and verified all fingerprints. Checked haulage tracks, locomotives, shuttle cars, trucks, signals, and rolling stock in sub 1, underground gasoline-engine safeguards referencing section 293.120 limits in sub 2, locomotive/car riding restrictions and exceptions in sub 3, director-set man-trip speed and capacity limits in sub 4, and uniform haulage signals and traffic control systems in sub 5. Retained all 5 drafted titles.

headings.title: Clearance and guarding of surface overhead power lines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 16). Requires surface overhead high-potential power lines to be at least 15 feet above ground and 20 feet above driveways and haulageways, mounted on insulators, and guarded against contact with other circuits.

headings.title: Lightning, surge, and high-potential line overcurrent protection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 16). Requires lightning and voltage-surge protection on surface overhead power circuits and circuit breakers, fuses, or both on high-potential power lines.

headings.title: Fire and contact safety for wiring, machinery, and lights
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 16). Requires electric wiring, stationary electrical machinery, and electric lights in mines and surface buildings to be installed and maintained to minimize fire and contact hazards.

headings.title: Periodic operator examinations and reports on electrical equipment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 16). Directs the division of mine inspection to require operators in all mines to make systematic, periodic examinations and reports on wiring and electrical equipment conditions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 16) and verified all fingerprints. Checked 15-ft/20-ft clearance and guarding of surface overhead high-potential lines in sub 1, lightning/surge protection on surface overhead circuits and circuit breakers/fuses on high-potential power lines in sub 2, fire/contact safety in mines and surface buildings in sub 3, and division-mandated periodic operator electrical examinations/reports in sub 4. Revised sub 2 title to avoid restricting high-potential line overcurrent protection solely to surface lines; retained subs 1, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Grounding of metal conduit and cable armor
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 17). Requires metal conduit and metallic cable coverings and armor to be grounded and electrically continuous to provide a ground-circuit conductor path.

headings.title: Grounding of metallic frames and equipment casings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 17). Requires grounding of metallic frames, casings, and other electrical equipment that can become energized through insulation failure.

headings.title: Grounding or isolation of transformer casings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 17). Requires transformer casings to be grounded unless protected by isolation or positioned free from contact hazard.

headings.title: Grounding of mobile equipment using trailing cables
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 17). Requires effective grounding of mining equipment mounted on rubber tires or caterpillar treads powered through a trailing cable.

headings.title: Guarding of trolley and positive feed wires
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 17). Requires trolley and positive feed wires crossing travelways used by persons or animals to be safely guarded or protected.

headings.title: Nonconductive platforms and mats at switches and machinery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 17). Requires dry wooden platforms, rubber mats, or other nonconductive materials at switchboards, power control switches, and stationary machinery presenting shock hazards.

headings.title: Overload fuses, prohibited substitutes, and circuit breakers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 17). Requires properly rated, accessible fuses or equivalent overload protection, bars substituting wires or conductors for fuses, and requires proper maintenance and adjustment of circuit breakers.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 7 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 17) and verified all fingerprints. Verified grounding of conduit/cable armor (sub 1), frames/casings (sub 2), transformer casings with isolation/position exception (sub 3), trailing-cable mobile equipment (sub 4), guarding of trolley/positive feed wires (sub 5), nonconductive platforms/mats (sub 6), and overload fuses, substitute prohibition, and circuit-breaker maintenance (sub 7). Retained all 7 drafted titles.

headings.title: Adequate firefighting equipment for each mine
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 17). Requires every mine to have suitable firefighting equipment adequate for its size and type of operations.

headings.title: Fireproof storage and metal containers for combustibles and lubricants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 17). Requires fireproof construction for underground storage of highly combustible material, lubricating oil, and grease, and requires portable, closed metal containers for oil and grease kept in face regions or working places.

headings.title: Fireproof construction for underground structures, stations, and pumprooms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 17). Requires fireproof construction for underground structures, transformer stations, battery-charging stations, substations, and permanent pumprooms.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 17) and verified all fingerprints. Verified mine firefighting equipment in sub 1, fireproof underground combustible/lubricant storage and closed metal working-place containers in sub 2, and fireproof construction for underground structures, transformer stations, battery-charging stations, substations, and permanent pumprooms in sub 3. Revised sub 3 title to include general 'underground structures' alongside stations and pumprooms; retained subs 1-2.

headings.title: Protective hats underground and on surface, with exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 18). Requires all persons to wear protective hats underground and in surface falling-object hazard areas, except where conditions would subject the wearer to physical hardship.

headings.title: Protective footwear in falling-object areas, with exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 18). Requires employees, officials, and others on duty in and around mines to wear protective footwear where falling objects may cause injury, subject to a physical-hardship exception.

headings.title: Approved goggles for flying-particle hazards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 18). Requires all employees in or around mines to wear approved-type goggles where flying-particle hazards exist.

headings.title: Eye shields or goggles for welders and helpers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 18). Requires welders and helpers to use proper eye-protection shields or goggles.

headings.title: Respiratory gear and other controls for inhalation hazards
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 18). Requires permissible respiratory equipment for short-period exposure to gas, dust, fumes, or mist, and requires other protective or hazard-reduction measures for prolonged exposure.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 18) and verified all fingerprints. Checked protective hats and footwear with their physical-hardship exceptions (subs 1-2), approved goggles for flying particles (sub 3), welder/helper eye shields or goggles (sub 4), and short-period respiratory gear plus prolonged-exposure controls (sub 5). Retained all 5 drafted titles.

headings.title: Dual outlets and passageways for shaft coal mines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 20, 21). Prohibits working a shaft coal mine without at least two separate outlets separated by at least 300 feet of natural strata per worked seam (allowing shared connection to another mine) and a clean, safely sized connecting roadway.

headings.title: Escapement shaft appliances and hoist availability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 20, 21). Requires safe, maintained escape appliances in escapement shafts, excludes air shafts with bottom ventilating furnaces from qualifying as escapement shafts, and requires cages/egress to remain available whenever no second outlet exists.

headings.title: Dual-outlet deadline and worker limit for slopes and drifts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 20, 21). Requires slope or drift coal mines to provide two outlets within 12 months after coal shipments begin, and bars permitting more than five workers at once if outlets are not provided as stipulated.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties for outlet violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 20, 21). Makes coal mine owner, agent, or operator violations a misdemeanor punishable by a $50-$200 fine, 3-12 months county jail imprisonment, or both.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 20, 21) and verified all fingerprints. Checked dual outlets/300-ft natural strata and connecting roadways for shaft coal mines in sub 1, escapement appliances, bottom-furnace air-shaft exclusion, and cage availability in sub 2, 12-month dual-outlet deadline and five-person limit for slope/drift coal mines in sub 3, and owner/agent/operator misdemeanor penalties in sub 4. Retained all 4 drafted titles.

headings.title: Minimum ventilation in shaft, slope, or drift coal mines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 22, 23). Requires at least 100 cubic feet of circulating air per minute per worker (increasable by the director) forced to every working face in every shaft, slope, or drift coal mine. Note: official catchline refers to "Shaft coal mines," while subsection 1 text covers shaft, slope, or drift coal mines.

headings.title: Self-closing main-entry doors and trappers for fifty or more
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 22, 23). Requires main-entry ventilation doors to be tight and self-closing, and requires a trapper in attendance in mines employing 50 or more men.

headings.title: Director notice and authority to order miners out
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 22, 23). Requires the director, upon finding men working without sufficient air or in unsafe conditions, to give the operator reasonable notice to rectify and authorizes ordering workers out upon refusal until corrected.

headings.title: Ventilation appliances and fireproofing for ventilating furnaces
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 22, 23). Permits ventilation by suitable appliances and requires any ventilating furnace to prevent fire spread by lining the upcast with incombustible material for a sufficient distance.

headings.title: Splitting air currents for worker groups
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 22, 23). Requires splitting coal-mine air currents to give a separate current to at least every 50 working men, with director discretion to require separate currents for smaller groups under special conditions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 22, 23) and verified all fingerprints. Verified catchline-vs-body scope in sub 1 (catchline names 'Shaft coal mines' while text covers every shaft, slope, or drift coal mine), 50-or-more-men trapper threshold on main-entry doors in sub 2, director notice and discretionary removal order upon refusal in sub 3, ventilation appliances and furnace-upcast fireproofing in sub 4, and 50-worker air-current splitting with director discretion in sub 5. Revised sub 1 title to specify shaft, slope, or drift coal mines and sub 2 title to reflect the 50-or-more threshold for trappers; retained subs 3-5.

headings.title: Locked explosive strongboxes and placement distance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 28, 29). Requires coal mine owners, agents, or operators to mandate locked strongboxes for surplus powder or explosives (beyond immediate use), positioned at least 100 feet from blasting places.

headings.title: Shot firers in gassy or solid-blasting coal mines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 28, 29). Requires operators of dry and dusty coal mines discharging light carbonated hydrogen gas, or mines blasting coal off the solid, to employ shot firers to fire all shots after employees and others have left the mine.

headings.title: Safe shot preparation and condemning dangerous shots
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 28, 29). Requires safe drilling and charging of solid-coal shots and directs shot firers to condemn and skip firing any gripping, "tight," windy, blown-out, or otherwise dangerous shot.

headings.title: Reporting and remedying condemned shots
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 28, 29). Requires shot firers to notify the mine foreman of condemned shots, the foreman to notify responsible miners, and those miners to immediately render condemned shots harmless upon returning to work.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties for owner, agent, or operator violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 28, 29). Makes coal mine agent, owner, or operator violations a misdemeanor punishable by a $100-$250 fine, 6 months to 1 year county jail imprisonment, or both in a court of competent jurisdiction.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 28, 29) and verified all fingerprints. Checked locked explosive strongboxes and 100-ft distance in sub 1, shot firers in dry/dusty gassy or solid-blasting coal mines in sub 2, shot preparation and condemning dangerous shots in sub 3, reporting and remedying condemned shots in sub 4, and misdemeanor penalties applying to coal mine agents, owners, or operators violating any provision of section 293.260 in sub 5. Revised sub 5 title to specify owner, agent, or operator violations across the section rather than only blasting; retained subs 1-4.

headings.title: Shaft signalmen hours and ascending cages for miners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 37). Requires coal mines employing 25 or more men to station competent signalmen at shaft top and bottom from 30 minutes before coal hoisting starts until 30 minutes after it ends, and requires furnishing an empty ascending cage whenever eight finished or prevented workers present themselves at the shaft bottom.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties for knowing violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 37). Makes knowing violations by coal mine owners, agents, or operators a misdemeanor punishable by a $100-$300 fine, 30-90 days county jail imprisonment, or both.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 37) and verified all fingerprints. Verified 25-or-more-men shaft signalmen hours and eight-person ascending-cage trigger in sub 1 and knowing violation misdemeanor penalties for coal mine owners, agents, or operators in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Twice-weekly hoisting inspections and employee-accessible logbook
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 39, 41). Requires coal mines employing 25 or more miners/laborers using mechanical hoisting devices for personnel to have an experienced practical person inspect ropes, cages, safety catches, shive wheels, and drum brakes at least twice weekly and record dated results in an on-site book open to all employees on working days.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties and separate daily offenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 39, 41). Makes noncompliance with subsection 1 a misdemeanor punishable by a $25-$100 fine, 30-90 days county jail imprisonment, or both, with each day's failure to inspect and record constituting a separate offense.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 39, 41) and verified all fingerprints. Verified twice-weekly mechanical hoisting inspections and employee-accessible logbook for coal mines employing 25 or more in sub 1 and misdemeanor penalties with separate daily offenses in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Room-and-pillar parallel entries, crosscuts, and abandoned mouths
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 42, 43). For room-and-pillar coal mines employing five or more persons, requires parallel entries, crosscuts no more than 50 feet apart, no openings inside the last crosscut until the next is made, and bars leaving abandoned room or entry mouths open more than one month.

headings.title: Discretionary sealing of abandoned rooms and entries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 42, 43). Requires secure gas-tight sealing of designated abandoned work, qualified by a proviso limiting sealing to mines and places where the director of mine inspection deems it necessary for worker health and safety.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties and daily subsequent offenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 42, 43). Makes noncompliance in room-and-pillar coal mines a misdemeanor punishable by a $100-$1,000 fine, 6 months to 1 year county jail imprisonment, or both, with each day of noncompliant operation after a first conviction constituting a separate subsequent offense.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 42, 43) and verified all fingerprints. Verified room-and-pillar five-or-more-person parallel entries, 50-ft crosscuts, and one-month abandoned-mouth limit in sub 1, gas-tight sealing qualified by the director-discretion proviso in sub 2, and misdemeanor penalties with daily post-conviction subsequent offenses in sub 3. Retained all 3 drafted titles.

headings.title: Director-approved minimum standards for systematic roof control
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 44). Requires coal mine operators to compile minimum systematic roof-control standards, place them in effect upon the director's written approval, ensure compliance, and install additional supports where necessary.

headings.title: Operator supply of timber and roof-bolting materials
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 44). Requires coal mine operators to provide ample timber, cap pieces or wedges, roof-bolting materials, or other proper roof-securing devices.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 44) and verified all fingerprints. Verified director-approved minimum systematic roof-control standards and additional supports in sub 1 and operator supply of timber, cap pieces/wedges, roof-bolting materials, or other devices in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Prohibiting excessive coal dust and allaying dust at source
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 45). Prohibits operators from permitting excessive coal dust accumulation and requires water, wetting agents, or other effective methods to allay excessive operational dust at its source.

headings.title: Rock-dusting requirements, wet-dust exceptions, and drying areas
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 45). Requires rock-dusting coal mines to within 40 feet of active faces and open crosscuts in that zone, exempts mines or locations too wet or high in incombustible content to propagate explosions, and mandates rock-dusting wet areas once they dry.

headings.title: Rock-dust coverage and minimum incombustible content
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 45). Requires applying rock dust to top, floor, and sides of open places in quantities maintaining at least 65% incombustible mine-dust content.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 45) and verified all fingerprints. Verified excessive coal-dust prohibition and source allaying in sub 1, 40-ft rock-dusting with wet/incombustible exceptions and drying-area rule in sub 2, and top/floor/sides coverage at 65% minimum incombustible content in sub 3. Retained all 3 drafted titles.

headings.title: Payment by weight, scale testing, records, and exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 47). Requires paying coal miners by weight, semiannual scale testing and repair, miner-accessible weighing records, and director-prescribed U.S. test weights, while exempting operators employing no more than three men at once and excluding mechanical miners paid a collective-bargaining day rate.

headings.title: Prohibition on pre-weighing coal screening or removal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 47). Bars operators from screening coal or removing any part before weighing and requires crediting just and merchantable weight to the employee.

headings.title: Weighmaster qualifications, no-interest affidavit, and posting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 47). Requires weighmasters to demonstrate scale competency to the mine inspector, swear an affidavit of no financial interest and accurate weighing, file it with the county circuit clerk, and post a copy conspicuously at the weighing place.

headings.title: Miner-employed check-weighmaster rights and qualifications
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 47). Empowers coal miners to employ a check-weighmaster at their own expense to observe weighing, test scales, and inspect records, subject to the same qualifications, oath, and penalties as the weighmaster.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 47) and verified all fingerprints. Verified payment by weight, semiannual scale testing, miner-accessible records, U.S. test weights, <=3-men operator exemption, and collective-bargaining mechanical-miner day-rate exclusion in sub 1, pre-weighing screening/removal ban in sub 2, weighmaster qualifications, no-interest affidavit, filing, and posting in sub 3, and miner-employed check-weighmaster rights and qualifications in sub 4. Retained all 4 drafted titles.

headings.title: Division authority to inspect coal-mine weighing equipment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 47). Designates the division of mine inspection as inspector of weights and measures at all coal mines and directs frequent inspections of scales, instruments, cars, containers, and operator competency.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for refusing scale tests or adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 47). Makes refusal to permit scale testing or failure to adjust scales after inspector notice a misdemeanor punishable by up to a $500 fine, up to 6 months county jail, or both, with prosecution by county prosecuting attorneys.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalty for fraudulent coal weighing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 47). Makes rigging scales or knowingly causing incorrect weighing or reporting of coal miners' output contrary to sections 293.420 and 293.430 a misdemeanor punishable by a $200-$500 fine, up to 90 days county jail, or both.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 47) and verified all fingerprints. Verified division weights-and-measures inspection authority at coal mines in sub 1, misdemeanor penalty and county prosecution for refusing scale tests or adjustments in sub 2, and misdemeanor penalty for fraudulent weighing contrary to sections 293.420 and 293.430 in sub 3. Retained all 3 drafted titles.

headings.title: One-hour surface meal and rest break and free hoisting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 49, 50). Requires underground coal mine owners, lessees, and operators to allow miners and laborers at least one hour on the surface for scheduled meals and rest, and to provide cage or hoisting transport to and from the surface free of cost.

headings.title: Misdemeanor fine for meal-period violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 49, 50). Makes failure or refusal to comply with section 293.450 a misdemeanor punishable by a $1-$25 fine, with each failure or refusal constituting a separate offense.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 §§ 49, 50) and verified all fingerprints. Checked combined minimum one-hour surface meal and rest period plus free cage/hoisting transport for underground coal miners in sub 1 and $1-$25 misdemeanor fines with separate offenses in sub 2. Revised sub 1 title to clarify a combined one-hour meal and rest break rather than a separate one-hour rest; retained sub 2.

headings.title: Fifteen-day wage payment cycle and five-day withholding limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 53). Requires coal mine operators to pay employees every 15 days in lawful U.S. money without withholding earnings due, subject to a proviso allowing withholding of up to five days' earnings.

headings.title: Double-wage civil liability for unpaid coal-miner wages
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 53). Makes nonpaying coal-mine operators or employers immediately liable in a civil action for double the unpaid wages due to the employee or an authorized collector.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 53) and verified all fingerprints. Verified 15-day coal-miner wage payment cycle in lawful U.S. money with five-day withholding proviso in sub 1 and double-wage civil liability for nonpayment in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Reporting intention before opening new mines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 57). Prohibits opening new mines or mining property without first reporting the intention and director-required pertinent information to the director.

headings.title: Ten-day notice of abandonment, resumption, name, or owner change
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 57). Requires operators to notify the director within 10 days after permanent mine abandonment, post-abandonment resumption of work, or change in mine name or owner.

headings.title: Sealing or fencing openings of abandoned underground mines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 57). Requires operators abandoning an underground mine to seal or fence surface openings to provide permanent protection to persons and animals.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 57) and verified all fingerprints. Verified pre-opening report to director in sub 1, 10-day notice of permanent abandonment, resumption, or change in mine name or owner in sub 2, and sealing or fencing abandoned underground mine openings in sub 3. Revised sub 2 title to include mine name changes alongside ownership changes; retained subs 1 and 3.

headings.title: Air current requirement for underground noncoal mines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 59). Requires operators of underground mines other than coal mines to maintain an air current sufficient to remove smoke and noxious gases and protect employee health and safety.

headings.title: Natural or mechanical ventilation appliances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 59). Requires controlling noncoal-mine ventilation by natural or mechanical appliances, or both if deemed necessary by the director.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 59) and verified all fingerprints. Verified air-current mandate for underground noncoal mines in sub 1 and natural or mechanical ventilation appliances (or both if deemed necessary by the director) in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Noncoal surface magazine construction, security, and location
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 62). Sets bulletproof, incombustible, wood-lined steel-door, locking, warning-sign, and 200-foot distance (unless barricaded) requirements for separate surface magazines storing explosives and detonators at noncoal mines.

headings.title: Underground section boxes and separate detonator storage
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 62). Sets construction, placement-distance (25 feet from roadways/trolley wires and 200 feet from active working places), dryness, and separation requirements for underground explosive and detonator boxes or magazines.

headings.title: Prohibition on black blasting powder underground
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 62). Prohibits transporting, storing, or using black blasting powder in underground mines.

headings.title: Fourteen-day underground explosive supply limit and adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 62). Requires noncoal mine operators to set maximum underground explosive supplies not exceeding estimated 14-day needs, unless a lesser or greater amount is approved or ordered by the director.

headings.title: Prohibition on storing explosives near escape routes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 62). Prohibits storing explosives anywhere in a mine where accidental discharge would cut off or obstruct miners' escape.

headings.title: Director rules for storing, handling, and using explosives
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 62). Requires mine explosive and detonator storage, movement, charging, firing, and use not otherwise specified in section 293.580 to follow director-prescribed rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 6 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 62) and verified all fingerprints. Checked noncoal surface magazine standards and 200-ft barricaded exception in sub 1, underground section boxes and separate detonator storage in sub 2, underground black blasting powder ban in sub 3, 14-day supply cap with director approval/order adjustment in sub 4, escape-route storage prohibition in sub 5, and director rules for other explosive handling in sub 6. Revised sub 1 title to state noncoal applicability explicitly; retained subs 2-6.

headings.title: Hoisting engineers, safety controls, brakes, and indicators
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 63, A.L. 1967 p. 407). Requires a qualified hoisting engineer continuously on duty when men are underground in hoist-served noncoal mines, overspeed/overtravel/automatic-stop controls, holding brakes, and a visible cage-position indicator unless always in view.

headings.title: Hoisting rope standards, replacement, fastening, and splicing ban
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (1959-1967). Requires wire ropes meeting referenced "America Standard Association's Wire Rope Standards" (retaining source spelling verbatim), replacement after six broken wires per lay, drum-turn rules for conventional drum hoists, socket or thimble-and-clamp fastening, and a ban on spliced ropes.

headings.title: Daily hoisting inspections and employee-accessible logbook
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (1959-1967). Requires daily inspection of hoisting equipment by a trained inspector and an inspection record book open to all mine employees.

headings.title: Cage construction, gates, handholds, and single-cable safeties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (1959-1967). Requires steel bonnets, enclosed sides, end gates during personnel hoisting, handholds/chains, adequate floors, and director-approved spring catches or safety devices for single-cable cages.

headings.title: Posted passenger limits and cage weight-strength ratio
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 5 and source notes (1959-1967). Directs the director or inspector to set and post maximum cage passenger numbers at all landings, capped so cage plus riders (160 lbs each) does not exceed one-fifth of minimum breaking strength.

headings.title: Separating riders from freight and securing small tools
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 6 and source notes (1959-1967). Restricts riding cages or trips carrying explosives, steel, equipment, or material to an attendant, and requires securing small hand tools, lunch containers, and small parts to director approval.

headings.title: High-speed cage approvals, test runs, records, and cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 7 and source notes (1959-1967). Requires director approval, thorough inspection, and two full-load test runs for personnel cage speeds over 500 feet per minute (and after major repairs or installations, recorded in an employee-accessible book), caps speed at 1,500 feet per minute, and requires posting safe speeds at landings.

headings.title: Inspector-approved underground hoisting signaling code
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 8 and source notes (1959-1967). Requires every mine hoisting or lowering men underground to adopt an adequate signaling code subject to mine-inspector approval.

headings.title: Shift-change shaft signalmen for mines employing twenty-five or more
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 9 and source notes (1959-1967). Requires mines employing 25 or more men to station competent signalmen at shaft top and bottom at shift beginnings and ends to answer and control hoisting signals.

headings.title: Exemption for mines employing fewer than sixteen underground
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 10 and source notes (1959-1967). Exempts mines employing fewer than 16 men underground from section 293.590.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 10 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 63, A.L. 1967 p. 407) and verified all fingerprints. Checked noncoal hoisting engineers/controls/brakes/indicators in sub 1, hoisting rope rules in sub 2 (retaining archived spelling 'America Standard Association's Wire Rope Standards' verbatim), daily inspections and logbook in sub 3, cage construction and single-cable safeties in sub 4, posted passenger limits and 1/5 breaking-strength ratio in sub 5, freight/rider separation and secured small tools in sub 6, high-speed (>500 fpm) approvals/test runs/1,500 fpm cap in sub 7, signaling code in sub 8, shift-change shaft signalmen for mines employing 25+ in sub 9, and the exemption for mines employing fewer than 16 underground in sub 10. Retained all 10 drafted titles.

headings.title: Annual public-cave inspections, safety rules, and plan maps
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 66). Directs the division of mine inspection to inspect public caves at least annually, adopt health and safety rules, require safety installations before public opening, and require filing a plan map with the division and at the cave entrance office.

headings.title: Opening notice, annual fee, and displayed inspection certificate
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 66). Requires written pre-opening notice, an annual $35 fee collected by DOR for the state mine inspection fund, and conspicuous entrance display of the division's inspection certificate upon compliance.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 66) and verified all fingerprints. Verified annual public-cave inspections, safety rules, pre-opening safety measures, and dual plan-map filing in sub 1, and written pre-opening notice, $35 annual fee to the state mine inspection fund, and conspicuous certificate display in sub 2. Retained both drafted titles.

headings.title: Mine inspector appointments, qualifications, salary, and conflicts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 4, A.L. 1967 p. 383, A.L. 1971 S.B. 65). Directs appointment of two coal and four noncoal mine inspectors with experience and safety-training qualifications, bars economic conflicts of interest, sets the archived $8,400 annual salary, and places inspectors under director supervision.

headings.title: Appointment and salaries of secretary and clerical employees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (1959-1971). Authorizes the director to appoint a secretary, one clerk, and necessary clerical employees for the inspection section and set their annual salaries within appropriations.

headings.title: Bipartisan balance in section appointments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (1959-1971). Requires appointees in each classification to be selected as nearly as practicable in equal numbers from the two political parties receiving the highest and second-highest gubernatorial votes at the last state election.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 4, A.L. 1967 p. 383, A.L. 1971 S.B. 65) and verified all fingerprints. Checked legacy 1971 statutory text setting coal/noncoal inspector appointments, qualifications, conflict bar, and archived $8,400 salary in sub 1, appointment and appropriation-limited salaries of a secretary, one clerk, and clerical employees for the 'inspection section' in sub 2, and bipartisan balance in each classification in sub 3. Revised sub 2 title to include the secretary alongside clerical employees; retained subs 1 and 3 as neutral archived-text descriptions.

headings.title: Minimum twice-yearly mine examinations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 8). Requires each Missouri mine to be examined by a mine inspector at least twice every calendar year, and more frequently if necessary or desirable to enforce chapter 293.

headings.title: Inspector entry rights, operator assistance, and enforcement orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 8). Authorizes day or night non-obstructive mine inspections, requires operators to furnish entry and inspection facilities, and allows inspectors to obtain circuit-court orders backed by contempt upon operator refusal.

headings.title: Scope of mine safety examinations and other duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 8). Directs inspectors to examine escapements, transportation, ventilation, air conditions, electricity, explosives, roof control, drainage, operations, and general security, plus other director-required duties.

headings.title: Inspector examination reports to director
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 4 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 8). Requires mine inspectors to submit mine examination reports to the director in the form and content prescribed by the director.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 8) and verified all fingerprints. Verified minimum twice-yearly examinations in sub 1, non-obstructive day/night entry, operator assistance, and circuit-court contempt orders in sub 2, safety examination scope and director-assigned duties in sub 3, and director-prescribed examination reports in sub 4. Retained all 4 drafted titles.

headings.title: Written dangerous-condition complaints, confidentiality, and required contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 11). Directs prompt mine inspection upon signed written complaint by mine employees or their certified bargaining agent alleging unlawful dangerous conditions, bars divulging complainant names except as needed in state courts, and requires specifying alleged violations, dangers, and prior notice to mine management.

headings.title: Inspector danger notices and remedial enforcement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 11). Directs an inspector finding dangerous conditions to serve a detailed written notice on the operator or person in charge and take remedial and compliance steps available under section 293.660.

headings.title: Forwarding and filing original complaints with division
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 3 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 11). Requires inspectors to forward every original complaint to the division of mine inspection for indexing and filing among official division papers.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 11) and verified all fingerprints. Verified written signed dangerous-condition complaints by mine employees or certified bargaining agents, confidentiality with state-court exception, and required complaint contents in sub 1, written danger notices and section 293.660 remedial enforcement in sub 2, and forwarding/indexing/filing original complaints with the division in sub 3. Retained all 3 drafted titles.

headings.title: Circuit court appeals, deadline, automatic stay, and notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 67). Allows any person to appeal orders, rules, regulations, or determinations of the director or a mine inspector within 30 days after notice in the mine's county or Cole County circuit court, automatically staying enforcement upon filing, with clerk-mailed notice and proof of mailing.

headings.title: Nonjury de novo trial and further civil appeal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete subsection 2 and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 67). Requires nonjury de novo circuit-court trial no sooner than 30 days after petition mailing, empowers the court to sustain the agency or direct proper action, and allows appeal as in civil actions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and source notes (L. 1959 S.B. 188 § 67) and verified all fingerprints. Verified 30-day circuit-court appeals (mine county or Cole County), automatic stay upon filing, and clerk-mailed notice in sub 1, and nonjury de novo trial no sooner than 30 days after mailing with civil appeal rights in sub 2.
